result:
No. I found no logout handler on the server, and nothing in the logout path touches the FCM token.

- A case-insensitive search of `src/` for `logout` returned no matches outside the FCM spec files. There's no server-side logout endpoint, so nothing there calls the FCM service.
- The only explicit removal is `DELETE /fcm/unregister-token/:deviceId` (`src/fcm/fcm.controller.ts:51-64`). It calls `unregisterDeviceToken`, which soft-deactivates the row by setting `isActive=false` and `deletedAt` (`src/fcm/fcm.service.ts:127-132`). The client has to call it itself. Nothing in this repo makes that call at logout.
- Registering a new token on login also deactivates the user's tokens. `registerDeviceToken` calls `unregisterAllDeviceTokens` (`fcm.service.ts:97-103`, `146-151`). This happens on the next register, not at logout. Until then the old token stays active, so pushes such as call and KYC notifications can still reach a logged-out device.
- `removeInvalidTokens` (`fcm.service.ts:283-284`) is the only hard delete, but it is private and has no callers (`fcm.service.ts:283` is its only match). Stale tokens are therefore never pruned after a send failure.

Whether tokens get removed at logout depends on the client calling `DELETE /fcm/unregister-token/:deviceId`. I can't tell from this repo whether it does.
